beur-hagra/2:ב: And even if it went out, etc. — for otherwise it would be forbidden on Shabbat with oils and wicks the Sages forbade, because if it goes out one is concerned and perhaps it will go out in such a case and one will transgress, as Rashi wrote there.
biur-halacha/1:ב: That if one uses, etc. — see Magen Avraham who wrote: nevertheless it is forbidden to use near them, etc. See Peri Megadim who explained even against the additional light or the sun it is forbidden l'chatchila; one who examines Rabbeinu Yerucham brought in Beit Yosef — it does not imply thus, only against the sun when he places it separately somewhat distant from the light it is permitted to use facing it; so Machatzit HaShekel in explanation of Magen Avraham's words — see there. I later found in Eliyah Rabbah who agreed likewise to the law that against the sun one may use. See in Sha'arei Teshuvah end d.h. haShamash — his view too is as we wrote.
chatam-sofer/1:_: In Magen Avraham s.k. 10. See Tosafot Zevachim 72a d.h. u'livatalo — they wrote: one could say the Mishnah Avodah Zarah 74a that we consider prohibition in the majority — one could say also in an open barrel because it is considered for idolatry — see there; but certainly once mixed and not recognizable it is no longer considered for idolatry; therefore after the fact we follow, as Terumat HaDeshen's words; see Plati siman 101 who brings proof from Pesachim 89 — his words require study for the examiner — end; see responsa Panim Me'irot part 4 siman 98 and Shevut Yaakov siman 32 — both intended the same thing [from the Gaon, may he live].
chokhmat-shlomo/1:_: Seif 1: Oils and wicks are valid for Hanukkah light, etc. NB: We have the text in Shas: all oils, etc. — one does not kindle with them on Hanukkah, whether weekday or Shabbat — he holds if it goes out one is concerned, and permitted to use its light. Tosafot questioned: from where does he hold permitted to use its light? Perhaps because if it goes out one is concerned; on Shabbat one cannot kindle — they answered: if so he should have said anonymously one does not kindle with them on Hanukkah; from "whether on Shabbat" it is proven on Shabbat there is another reason to forbid lest one tilt, etc. It appears unexplained why the Gemara teaches this, since for "if it goes out one is concerned" alone it is forbidden on Shabbat — why mention "whether on Shabbat"? One could say it teaches we may use its light — besides being strained to infer in the explanation "permitted to use its light," it is more difficult: Tosafot themselves wrote therefore Rav said one kindles whether weekday or Shabbat, not anonymously — for if he said anonymously one might think only weekday not Shabbat, as one might think no amora would hold forbidden to use its light; if the reasoning externally is permitted to use, until Rav had to inform us forbidden — if the view permitting use would not need to inform us, since reasoning is so no one would say forbidden to use its light. However the intent appears: from "one does not kindle with them on Hanukkah" anonymously it is proven even mehaderin do not kindle even in additional lights; it is difficult: since we hold in many places where b'dieved valid without this, l'chatchila no concern lest one forget — granted for one light, since he holds if it goes out one is concerned, b'dieved he does not fulfill Hanukkah, therefore concern lest he forget to relight; but for mehaderin's light, b'dieved if he forgets there is no stringency — it should be permitted to kindle additional lights by mehaderin with these oils — why say anonymously one does not kindle with them on Hanukkah? However necessarily he holds permitted to use its light — therefore on Shabbat forbidden to kindle even additional, since permitted to use its light lest one tilt; therefore even weekday forbidden with these oils even in additional — if in additional permitted, they would say what on Shabbat we do not kindle from them is only because if it goes out one is concerned, and they would err to kindle additional on Shabbat like weekday; there is concern lest one tilt — therefore even weekday one does not kindle with them at all even in additional, lest Shabbat; and it is proven he holds permitted to use its light — otherwise on Shabbat additional with these oils would be permitted, and he would not say anonymously one does not kindle on Hanukkah — it is proven he holds permitted to use its light; Tosafot's question is settled — examine. (Same seif, Hagahah) It is customary in these lands to kindle with wax candles because their light is clear like oil. NB: In law, one who glued Hanukkah wax candles to the wall and afterward received olive oil — the great ones of the world disputed: Shevut Yaakov to finish with wax candles; Chacham Tzvi responsa siman 44 to the contrary. Since it is Torah and I must learn, I too the poor one answer with my portion. First to Zion: proof from sugya chapter 2 Shabbat on kindling versus placement — Tosafot wrote there practical difference if kindled accidentally. This is not difficult — one could say difference if it went out between kindling and placement; if kindling accomplishes mitzvah he already did mitzvah and we hold if it went out not concerned; if placement accomplishes mitzvah he has not yet done mitzvah and must relight. One could say they meant difference even for all, even for view if it goes out concerned. Also before placement for all if it goes out concerned even if kindling accomplishes mitzvah, for we need recognition it is for Hanukkah — we hold he held and stood with Hanukkah light and did nothing, as Gemara explains the viewer says for his need he kindled; therefore all the time he did not place, for all he is concerned. However difficult — one could say difference if he was kindling wax and afterward received olive oil: if kindling accomplishes mitzvah he already kindled and cannot kindle again; if placement accomplishes mitzvah he has not done mitzvah and must withdraw hand and kindle olive oil. From not writing thus it is proven like Shevut Yaakov. Therefore if placement accomplishes mitzvah, since he already began doing them he is not obligated to continue — therefore cannot say this difference — examine. Now Chacham Tzvi's words: what he rejected of Shevut Yaakov's proofs he rejected well; but for the reverse too there is no proof. From R' Nissim of Modena where there are remnants for eating — it is proven where there are no remnants he does not say bring another — this is not proof, for there it speaks needing delay until bringing another — we certainly do not say that, as explained Yevamot 39: any mitzvah we do not delay even if more ideal mitzvah — see there. However Shevut Yaakov speaks where no delay needed — one could say he must withdraw to do more ideal mitzvah. From end chapter Hotsi'u Lo — since he began with first offering, etc. — he himself saw that proof can be rejected — perhaps there the first was already valid. From what he brought Shevuot 11 and if he found another nicer, and from permitting garment to garment — all this can be rejected in one rejection: certainly where hidur is recognizable from the thing itself, one is obligated to beautify and seek better hidur even though he already began with another — the hidur is recognizable in the mitzvah itself; this we learn from "and I shall glorify Him" — certainly obligated even if already engaged with another not as nice, even where hidur is not in the mitzvah itself only from owners' obligation for ideal mitzvah — e.g. here no difference to viewer between olive oil and wax, only because miracle was with oil and similar to menorah — here hidur is not from mitzvah itself only from doer; nothing is learned from "and I shall glorify Him" — one who began with another need not leave to do separately even if more ideal — Chacham Tzvi's words are correct as separate matters. Therefore it appears for law like Shevut Yaakov, especially rabbinic matter — examine. (Same seif) And some permit use of sacred utensils, etc. NB: This view is very difficult from Yerushalmi Tur siman 681 brought: one may not make havdalah on Hanukkah light, forbidden to use its light; that view — they nevertheless benefit from its light for mitzvah use — why make havdalah on synagogue light which is also mitzvah light, forbidden weekday use, yet havdalah on it? All the more difficult for view of Acharonim that temporary sacred use is permitted — they would suit its light for this; from where require permanent suit? Perhaps Yerushalmi means permitted temporary use since its essence is not for illumination — we do not bless on it, similar to dead person's light: permitted to benefit since not made for light, no blessing — likewise Hanukkah not made to use its light, no havdalah. With this reject proof in siman 681 to kindle Hanukkah before havdalah from Yerushalmi Tur cited — see what is written there. For what is written here, this proof is also rejected — perhaps there he kindled for Hanukkah need, not yet blessed, wants havdalah on it then bless on Hanukkah — teaches even then forbidden since he did not kindle to use, only for Hanukkah — like dead person's light no blessing — such is correct — examine. What is forbidden to use its light — Ran wrote reason similar to menorah; so other poskim — see there. It appears difficult: explicit Mishnah a woman sifts wheat by light of the drawing well — proves holy light was permitted. I saw Tosafot Pesachim chapter 2 and Shabbat chapter 2 sensed this but on other matters — why stand on Kol Marei v'Reiach in Pesachim no me'ilah but isur applies, and what Shabbat chapter 1 priests kindle, etc. — why not mention from forbidding to use its light? Necessarily similar to menorah and isur applies; also their question from Yerushalmi implies even in menorah forbidden and sifting literally; what difficulty — in our Gemara dispute of amoraim whether permitted to use its light — end; requires study — examine.
chokhmat-shlomo/2:_: (Same, seif 2) Kindling accomplishes the mitzvah; therefore if it went out before its time passed he is not concerned for it, etc. NB: The wording is puzzling as Taz wondered; we wrote in our novellae in several ways; now it appears thus according to Beit Yosef's answer why in siman 672 they wrote permitted to benefit from Hanukkah lamp oil, and in siman 677 ruled opposite — Beit Yosef answers: if remainder from measure required for kindling, forbidden to use; if more than required measure remains, permitted to benefit. It appears one should add seasoning: since we hold nothing whose mitzvah was done and one violates me'ilah in it — therefore all burnt offerings, their ash is permitted; so too if kindled as measure and more remains, mitzvah was done, therefore permitted to benefit. But if remainder is required measure, mitzvah was not done, therefore forbidden. However Beit Yosef did not write this reason — since we hold kindling accomplishes mitzvah, if it went out not concerned; if so immediately upon kindling mitzvah was done — even if remainder is measure, mitzvah was done, therefore forbidden to benefit — he had to give another reason; see on this regarding a faded Torah scroll whether one may write secular on it — responsa to community in Autishan. At least accordingly one could say: generally we forbid leaving forbidden things lest stumbling; Pesachim chapter 1 dilution — see there; so too here appropriate to say if it went out within time he is concerned to relight immediately since forbidden to benefit, concern lest stumble — but one could say in rabbinic matters they were lenient. We find things they strengthened like Torah law — but this is one rabbinic matter; in two rabbinic matters certainly they did not strengthen like Torah. Therefore two matters "if it went out concerned": one the Gemara debates for Hanukkah law itself if obligated to relight as Hanukkah light — difference if must bless again; if from Hanukkah law he would bless like tefillin if knot broke; Maharsha brought Beit Yosef here: if went out unintentionally no need to bless — we hold if it went out not concerned; implies if concerned, must bless. On this the Gemara debates; this law does not depend on kindling versus placement accomplishing mitzvah; therefore not resolved from this — we hold if it went out not concerned, not obligated to relight from Hanukkah law. However from another reason he should be concerned since forbidden to benefit and needs burning — concern lest forget and benefit; from this no blessing required, only concern of stumbling. Similar siman 434 on checking after Pesach — no blessing since only stumbling concern — see there. If placement accomplishes mitzvah, mitzvah not yet done since he did not kindle measure; if d'oraisa forbidden to benefit, even Hanukkah they would strengthen to kindle immediately lest stumbling; but since kindling accomplishes mitzvah, immediately upon kindling mitzvah done — even d'oraisa permitted to benefit; again no Torah-like strengthening; all the more rabbinic prohibition on remainder beyond measure — if it went out not concerned even from stumbling concern, permitted to leave for other days — it fits well — examine. Explanation of difference if kindling versus placement: if kindling accomplishes mitzvah he does not kindle every moment only at start — necessarily enactment from "whatever is fit for mixing, mixing does not block" — since at start he did main mitzvah, afterward for remainder "fit for mixing" — at start of kindling his whole mitzvah was done since fit for mixing; but for placement, mitzvah is all time of placement — he placed constantly, did whole placement putting oil — mitzvah is all placement time; what "if it went out not concerned" — only because ones rachmana patrei, not obligated to trouble to relight; therefore no fulfillment, mitzvah not done, forbidden by law — such is correct. Another way to resolve: reason if it went out concerned or not depends on kindling versus placement l'shem mitzvah: for view kindling accomplishes mitzvah — he only kindles a moment, remainder burns by itself — intent as Bava Kamma chapter 1 regarding fire because of substance: what burns at first as if he kindled all then; therefore afterward measure burning is branch of mitzvah — in branch we say fit for mixing; for placement view, main mitzvah is what rests in place — all placement time is main mitzvah — in main mitzvah we do not say fit for mixing, as Rashbam Bava Batra chapter 1 — see there. Therefore if it went out concerned. However l'chatchila why not obligated to relight — necessarily reason is not from fit for mixing but enactment from start; no difference kindling versus placement l'shem mitzvah. One could say: in Torah Menachot if not mixed valid — if Torah valid b'dieved, rabbinic Hanukkah permitted l'chatchila; therefore depends on fit for mixing. This depends on dispute Gittin 65: R' Chisda holds whatever Rabbis enacted like Torah — one view only where Torah has parallel, not where Torah has no parallel; we hold minor even throwing pebble does not acquire for others — necessarily like R' Chisda; as Gemara answers partnership of alleys is rabbinic — where no Torah parallel, not enacted like Torah; therefore Gemara debate if kindling or placement — R' Chisda holds in all things enacted like Torah; if fit for mixing not blocking, l'chatchila still must kindle like Menachah — therefore not resolved from this — we hold if it went out not concerned from fit for mixing, since Torah valid b'dieved, rabbinic l'chatchila permitted; where no Torah parallel not enacted like Torah — this reason if it went out not concerned from fit for mixing; proven kindling accomplishes mitzvah, therefore not concerned — correct — examine. Mechaber tied them — examine well.
machatzit-hashekel/2:ג: For otherwise he would buy Hanukkah, etc. — meaning we say there: Shabbat light and Hanukkah light — Shabbat light comes first because of shalom bayit; meaning if he has only one light he takes it for Shabbat and does not kindle Hanukkah — Rava's statement 23a. Impossible permitted to eat by Hanukkah light — he should kindle for Hanukkah and eat by it, fulfilling Hanukkah and shalom bayit. Although in Talmudic times they kindled outside at house or courtyard entrance — then no shalom bayit if kindling for Hanukkah; for us kindling inside within twenty — Magen Avraham — truly siman 678 possible shalom bayit thus; must be from Gemara words; although in their days they kindled outside, nevertheless lest Hanukkah mitzvah be nullified he should kindle inside — even when kindling inside in Talmudic times he fulfilled when impossible, for in danger they said place on table, siman 671 seif 5; although in danger he needs another light to use, siman 671 — for recognition it is for mitzvah, as Ran there — nevertheless without another light nearby it implies he still fulfilled Hanukkah; only when possible another light is required l'chatchila for recognition. When he has only one light, lest Hanukkah be nullified he should kindle on table even though forbidden to eat by it. Magen Avraham below siman 677: nowadays kindling inside, although forbidden to eat by it, nevertheless kindle for Hanukkah and eat by it when impossible — as in danger he places on table even though he uses it — specifically for us who otherwise kindle inside: kindle for Hanukkah and leave on table like danger; although in danger another light needed when possible for recognition; when impossible Magen Avraham permits even without another, since only recognition; for us in Talmudic times kindling outside — if permitted to eat by Hanukkah, Magen Avraham would permit kindling inside on table even without another; but since forbidden to eat by Hanukkah, they did not want to permit kindling inside since main mitzvah is outside, and also eating by it; although in danger permitted when another light for recognition — without another, to permit kindling inside and eating by it without another light, they were not lenient.
magen-avraham/1:ז: Longer. The same if he places it higher than the other lights — see there (Bach, Maharil, Magen Tzvi).
mishnah-berurah/1:ב: (2) Valid for Hanukkah light — nevertheless mitzvah from the preferred: take for wick cotton or flax threads [Chayei Adam]. Fat or milk forbidden by Torah prohibition — forbidden to kindle Hanukkah from it, also forbidden to nullify in sixty to kindle from it [Peri Megadim]. Those accustomed on first day one, and from then add — the addition must resemble the main light; but those who make a light for each household member — one may kindle oil, another wax. Stolen oil — requires study if valid for Hanukkah [responsa She'elot uTeshuvot part 1 third edition siman 249].
mishnah-berurah/1:ו: (6) If he does not put, etc., his mitzvah — if he puts more, concern lest he tilt that Hanukkah light to use after the kindling measure, when permitted to benefit, as above siman 672 seif 2.
mishnah-berurah/1:מ: (13) Forbidden — likewise synagogue lights one does not use their light, even sacred use like at home, i.e. if he wants to pray Ma'ariv by them — all this if they did not burn half an hour, forbidden.
mishnah-berurah/1:צ: (18) The shamash in it, etc. — even many kindling, since each places his lights in a special place as above siman 671 seif 2 in Hagahah, must place shamash by each even if there is light on the table, lest he use by the lights.
mishnah-berurah/1:ש: (21) If mixed, etc. — meaning after kindling an act was done, then mixed [before kindling not forbidden, for designation for Hanukkah light is nothing]; afterward it went out within its measure time; Terumat HaDeshen ruled not nullified even in a thousand — take one from them to kindle and use; likewise while burning one may not take one to use its light — all because it is a counted thing; meaning even where they usually sell lights by weight, nevertheless mitzvah lights each night are counted; a counted thing is significant and not nullified.
peri-megadim/4:_: And there is Taz, Bach, Levush who answered: with another present it is permitted; Taz forbids with oils and wicks that do not last — in such a case even with another present forbidden; only with valid oils when another is present permitted to read, as siman 275 — see there. However what some permit temporary sacred use — specifically no recognition in temporary use, as written in letter 3; also no bizui in mitzvah; some forbid — there is bizui from mitzvah to mitzvah; some say kindling light to light is one mitzvah — Ran there. What I wrote in letter 3 — requires study — perhaps because Shabbat 22 teaches sukkah forbidden, thus bizui even not against Hanukkah; like light to light forbidden by some because of bizui mitzvah — likewise here; therefore Taz ruled temporary forbidden even from distance if not sacred use — still requires study.
rabbi-akiva-eiger/2:_: {Rama: Seif 2} If unintentional, he is not concerned for it. Maharshal siman 85 ruled in such a case he must return and kindle.
shaarei-teshuvah/1:_: Valid. Eliyah Rabbah wrote in the name of Sha'ar Ephraim and copied from Leket HaKemach thus, and in Machatzit HaShekel in his name: permitted even the opposite — in truth he forbids in his conclusion there to kindle Hanukkah lights forbidden to use its light — here only enjoyment of mitzvot, and mitzvot were not given for enjoyment — nevertheless forbidden to kindle with it although we do not hold like Razah who holds rabbinic mitzvot were given for enjoyment; one could say since Hanukkah requires measure — must put oil in lamp to kindle as measure — and since Torah prohibition forbidden to benefit, measure is crushed — therefore forbidden to kindle with orlah oil; and one could say specifically orlah which is among burnt offerings (see there) — but Torah prohibition which is buried, we do not say measure crushed; and one could say for all buried things they are not burned — there reason is because of ash, unlike Hanukkah kindling where there is no ash only wick ash, and wick was not forbidden to benefit. Nevertheless forbid: even if ash reason does not apply, the law all buried things are not burned is not nullified by nullifying reason, as Rivash siman 34; also when burning them "measure crushed" may apply — see there and Eliyah Zuta wondered — otherwise forbidden because of cooking in Torah prohibition — siman 318 s.k. 130 cooking after cooking — see there and Shevut Yaakov part 1 siman 38 asked on Or Zarua — Shevut Yaakov answered before forbidden matter becomes coals it is fit to eat through heat — even warming is called cooking for Torah prohibition (words wondrous to me — see there further); even if doubt no complete cooking, Or Zarua should have raised this concern — end; see Peri Megadim 14 siman 87; here siman that questioned Sha'ar Ephraim — this is tigun, and tigun Maharam Shif wrote in novellae Chullin is rabbinic; likewise in flour for meal general chapter 80 wrote in butter mixed with milk permitted to kindle — tigun has no Torah prohibition — see there in introduction; and one could say absorbed in pot forbidden to benefit returns and is expelled into butter and forbids it — that is absorbed of Torah prohibition does not forbid butter to benefit since one does not benefit from kindling this absorption, as we say regarding wheat pile — see introduction to Bach in Peri Megadim there; see Chayei Adam Pesach laws regarding wheat found in chicken; Magen Avraham expanded; Eliyah Rabbah brought briefly Shevut Yaakov — clear even if always accustomed to olive oil and came home without olive oil and began preparing with wax candles, he completes mitzvah with wax since already began — mitzvah from preferred, do not despise first, as Yoma 7 standing offering omer — similar Beit Yaakov siman 126 regarding chalitzah when adult came and they already began with minor — see there; Chacham Tzvi rejected proof here not called began mitzvah only preparation — glued candles to wall, etc.; therefore appears he must withdraw from wax even if glued, kindle olive oil — proof Yoma chapter Hotsi'u Lo first sends, etc. — he wrote at length: there since he began actual mitzvah he may not reject this for the other; but to fulfill mitzvah itself from preferred, etc.; Maharil holds did not fulfill with wax; even when practicing like Rama, reason olive oil not common — not so when available, no hesitation; no difference whether now accustomed to olive oil or not; Shevut Yaakov on hidur mitzvah until third — only when not yet begun mitzvah — not so; if one has etrog and friend brings nicer even free while holding first to bless — forbidden to leave first, chapter HaTadir we learned seasons passed — likewise when east lit one day; also if took non-hidur etrog to bless and before blessing friend brings nicer free — bless on first non-hidur, let matter rest — clear between etrog and Hanukkah and all mitzvot: bless on nicer hidur even if came last; Shevut Yaakov part 2 siman 35 somewhat defends — wrote this preparation is certainly great beginning as we say regarding haircut leaving cloth, etc.; nevertheless clear there he agrees one who wants mitzvah from preferred — permission is his; proofs in part 1 only say need not despise first mitzvah — see there; Eliyah Rabbah brought briefly — I saw fit to copy roots and reasons: if already began blessing, even olive oil ready before him, since he began blessing thus he completes; also doubt whether must bless anew as siman 206 — see there; likewise etrog; also appears etrog first day: non-hidur is his, took to bless, friend wants to give nicer on condition return — rely on Shevut Yaakov: gift on condition return helps, nevertheless better fulfill with his own; Chacham Tzvi seems to agree; Eliyah Rabbah in name of Sha'ar Ephraim — see Birkei Yosef doubts: since not for his need when kindling, only they will say not from mehaderin — do not decree; also each placed lights in special place; household recognition — so I am lenient; see siman 675 Beit Yosef in name of Mahari Abuhav — end; see Eliyah Zuta nevertheless appropriate one night wax one night oil — see there; from Shevut Yaakov where olive oil expensive — appears he disputes Sha'ar Ephraim not to kindle part olive part other oils; Shevut Yaakov there words mixed — so it is; Eliyah Rabbah: one held by gentiles cannot kindle candles should kindle one each night (meaning even if oil for eight days, not like mehaderin other nights, only one each night); Sha'ar Ephraim siman 39 not comparable to five wounds — nevertheless since here main mitzvah only one light and not so recognizable at kindling — see there as correct.
shaarei-teshuvah/3:_: Coins. Eliyah Rabbah; see Peri Chadash in name of Maharikash: walking by Hanukkah light to see lest he stumble — permitted, not obligated to close eyes — not called use; see responsa Penei Aryeh siman 47 — they forbade only use; whatever is not use, permitted to sit in house while Hanukkah lights burn — see there from Peri Chadash; truly so explained Magen Avraham below siman 678: nowadays buy for Hanukkah, in any case do not sit in darkness, etc.; from there also proof as Maharikash wrote: main shalom bayit is in walking lest stumble; see above siman 663 Magen Avraham s.k. 13-14 — see there.
turei-zahav/1:ו: That it is a counted thing. Written there in Terumat HaDeshen siman 103: although when selling they sell by weight, nevertheless mitzvah was a counted thing; nevertheless once mixed after kindling for mitzvah, now it is a counted thing in its essence; although for weekday it was not counted — he brings proof from Tosafot chapter 5 100a — and you would say: why in chapter Orlah piece of tamei sin-offering mixed in ten pure — it ascends and is nullified? They answer: kodashim are not considered fit for honor since only kohanim eat regularly without expectation of reward — thus even though generally fit for honor, afterward we follow even to leniency; all the more here to stringency — end. I greatly wonder at this great man who wrote without precision — on the contrary, proof from there: Tosafot wrote in chapter Orlah we follow what will be after nullification; why in chapter Orlah end (Yevamot 81) tamei sin-offering mixed in non-sacred does not ascend because after nullification fit for honor in it; but in beginning mixed in pure sin-offering pieces it ascends, not fit for honor, no kohanim honor in Temple — therefore ascends, for whatever is customarily counted, etc. — end; meaning we hold specifically what is counted everywhere; here in Hanukkah if Hanukkah nullifies in weekday majority it is not counted — weekday they do not use by counting — similar to beginning if tamei mixed among pure pieces it nullifies well; however I have another reason it is not nullified: there in Terumat HaDeshen the lamps were placed burning and one Hanukkah light between two shamash lights mixed — I say there is a difference: if Hanukkah fixed in place, two shamash mixed with it — not nullified since we hold fixed is like half and half; but if Hanukkah moved from fixation and mixed elsewhere between shamash, then nullified well in majority; also in Piskei Maharshal I saw he wrote: it appears no need to add one light for shamash as Ashkenaz custom, since he has light on table — your enactment ruined enactment — I expanded; if Hanukkah mixed in two shamash, one in two nullified — end; we do not know his reason; I think he meant there is ruin through shamash light — perhaps he would benefit from shamash and come to benefit from other Hanukkah lights; or perhaps he meant benefit from added light of Hanukkah lights — I already wrote no prohibition from this.
yad-ephraim/3:_: In Taz s.k. 3, and so implied in hints he did not mention disgrace, etc.; nevertheless this does not answer except what he questioned — what disgrace in lecturing coins; but still difficult why Rosh needed to say because it is near the light — he should answer simply Rava Ashi taught even temporary use is forbidden; therefore he wrote since Tur did not write "against," meaning Tur truly does not distinguish near light or not, therefore wrote language "to use alone" so one not accustomed to infer from R' Elazar's wording as Rosh wrote from R' Elazar — therefore Tur used "its light" to say R' Elazar who wrote against Hanukkah light is mere wording, not to infer near Hanukkah light is required; if so, this is opposite Beit Yosef who questioned Tur should be like Rosh; on this Taz at start of his words: I find Rosh's words difficult, etc. — meaning on the contrary Rosh is difficult why he wrote thus, Tur truly did not write thus, and he should answer simply R' Elazar taught all temporary use forbidden.
